From: Ari Kaplan <ari@scalebridge.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: SDK stability and versioning commitments for ScaleBridge integration

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. ScaleBridge is ready to move forward with a pilot integration, but before we commit engineering cycles our platform team asked for clearer guarantees around SDK/API stability. Specifically we need:

- A minimum deprecation notice window for breaking changes (we're asking for 12 months).
- A promise that minor releases will be backward compatible for at least two minor versions (semver-like behavior).
- A list of API surface areas that may change in a non-backward-compatible way over the next 12 months (we can consume this for risk analysis).

Our concern is that we deeply integrate Redwood SDKs into our provisioning flows; frequent breaking changes force us to fork or add brittle shims. Is Redwood able to commit to a formal versioning/deprecation policy for partner integrations? If not a contract clause, a documented SLA/compatibility matrix would help.

We'd also like to request a short compatibility shim or migration guide if you anticipate deprecations in the next two quarters. I can share our integration matrix (I attached a one-pager) and propose follow-ups.

Thanks — can we sync early next week (Mon/Tue) for 30 minutes?

— Ari
Ari Kaplan
Head of Integrations, ScaleBridge Consulting
ari@scalebridge.com
+1 415-555-0197

Ari —

Appreciate the clear ask and the context. Welcome news that you're ready to pilot. Short answers first: yes, we can put a documented policy in place; the ask for a contractual 12-month minimum is something we'll need to route through Legal/Revenue, but technically we can commit to a formal rollout plan and compatibility shims for most client-facing surface areas.

Proposed next steps from our side:

1) Short-term (this week): share an internal compatibility matrix for the Redwood SDKs and list of endpoints that are considered "experimental" vs "stable" — attached as a working spreadsheet.
2) Near-term (2–4 weeks): engineering will evaluate effort to provide a compatibility shim for the SDK call patterns you indicated; if feasible we will publish a migration guide and a fallback adapter.
3) Contract/legal: I'll loop in RevOps to discuss a formal deprecation window for Partner customers if your pilot progresses to paid committed capacity.

I've asked Karthik (engineer on serving/runtime) and Camila (product partnerships) to join the call to cover technical and commercial details. Can you do Monday 12/7 at 10:00 PT or Tuesday 12/8 at 11:00 PT? 30 minutes.

Attaching the integration matrix you can edit: scalebridge-integration-matrix.xlsx (working draft).

Thanks —

Subject: Re: SDK stability and versioning commitments for ScaleBridge integration

Ari —

Quick technical reply based on the endpoints you flagged in the matrix:

- Our text-generation streaming API (vX) is stable and we guarantee no breaking change to the wire protocol for major+minor pinned clients for 6 months from release. For the 12-month ask, we can extend this for partners via a compatibility branch or a thin shim in the SDK.

- The primary risk areas are: function-calling payload schema, low-level tokenizer updates, and any kernel-level optimizations that change KV cache behavior. Each risk has different mitigation cost:
  * function-calling schema: low — we'll maintain a compatibility layer that maps old fields to new ones for two minor versions.
  * tokenizer updates: medium — we recommend pinning tokenizer binary in your build or using our tokenizer adapter available in the SDK.
  * KV/cache semantics: higher — requires a shim at the runtime call boundary; I attached a short patch proposal that implements a compatibility mode for older session tokens.

Plan proposal:
1) We deliver a compatibility shim (patch attached) that you can include in your integration. This gives you 12 months of behavior parity.
2) We publish an "API stability table" in the SDK docs and tag stable vs experimental endpoints.
3) For any contract-level guarantees we align with Laura/RevOps.

I'll be on the call Monday 12/7 10:00 PT. If you want a technical pre-read, see the attached patch and our versioning doc.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
